questions.question: Which of the following lakes is located in Buldhana district of Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lonar**__

__
 
• **Lonar** Lake is located in the Buldhana district of Maharashtra.
 
• It is a saline soda lake, created by a meteor impact during the Pleistocene Epoch.
 
• The lake is one of the four known hyper-velocity impact craters in basaltic rock anywhere on Earth.
 
• The crater has a mean diameter of 1.2 kilometers and is about 137 meters below the crater rim.
 
• Lonar Lake is also known for its unique ecosystem, which includes various algae, plankton, and microbial life forms that thrive in its high-salinity environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lonar Lake** has been a subject of scientific studies due to its unique geological and ecological features.
 
• The lake is surrounded by a variety of flora and fauna, making it a significant site for biodiversity.
 
• It is also a popular tourist destination and is considered a geological wonder.
 
• The lake has been declared a National Geo-heritage Monument by the Geological Survey of India.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to preserve and protect the lake from pollution and other environmental threats.

questions.question: What is the freezing point of water on the Celsius scale?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0ºC**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The freezing point of water on the Celsius scale is **0ºC**.
 
• The Celsius scale, also known as the centigrade scale, is a temperature scale used by the International System of Units (SI).
 
• On this scale, the freezing point of water is 0 degrees Celsius, and the boiling point is 100 degrees Celsius, under standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• The Celsius scale is widely used around the world for most temperature measuring purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Celsius scale was named after the Swedish astronomer **Anders Celsius**, who developed a similar temperature scale.
 
• Before being widely adopted, various temperature scales like Fahrenheit and Kelvin were also used for different purposes.
 
• The Celsius scale is particularly convenient for scientific calculations and everyday temperature measurements.
 
• In the Fahrenheit scale, the freezing point of water is 32ºF, and the boiling point is 212ºF.

questions.question: In dravidian style of temples the main temple tower is known as ___________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vimana**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Dravidian style of temples, the main temple tower is known as **vimana**.
 
• The **vimana** is the sanctum sanctorum where the main deity is enshrined and is usually topped with a dome-like structure.
 
• The **gopuram** is the monumental entrance tower, typically ornate, found at the entrance of the temple complex.
 
• The **mandapa** refers to the pillared hall or pavilion for public rituals and ceremonies.
 
• The **shikhara** is a term used in the Nagara style of temple architecture, referring to the rising tower in the sanctum sanctorum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Dravidian style** of temple architecture is prominent in South India.
 
• This architectural style evolved under the patronage of various South Indian dynasties such as the Cholas, Pallavas, and Pandyas.
 
• Characteristic features of Dravidian temples include large gopurams, intricate carvings, and expansive temple complexes.
 
• Famous examples of Dravidian temples include the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur and the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai.

questions.question: What is the primary function of carbohydrates in the body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide energy**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary function of carbohydrates in the body is **to provide energy**.
 
• Carbohydrates are broken down into glucose, which is the main source of fuel for the body's cells, tissues, and organs.
 
• Glucose can be used immediately or stored in the liver and muscles for later use.
 
• Carbohydrates are essential for maintaining proper brain function and physical activity.
 
• They are found in foods like bread, rice, pasta, fruits, and vegetables.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• While carbohydrates are a primary energy source, they also play a role in the structure of cells and the synthesis of DNA and RNA.
 
• There are two types of carbohydrates: simple and complex. Simple carbohydrates are quickly digested and provide a rapid source of energy, while complex carbohydrates provide sustained energy.
 
• Excess carbohydrates that are not used for energy are stored as fat in the body.
 
• A balanced diet with the right amount of carbohydrates is crucial for overall health and well-being.

questions.question: Sahel is an area in Africa that has lost a huge area of productive land in the last century due to excessive human activities and climate change. This area is a blaring example of _______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**desertification**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Desertification** is the process by which fertile land becomes desert, typically as a result of drought, deforestation, or inappropriate agriculture.
 
• The **Sahel** region in Africa has experienced significant desertification due to **excessive human activities and climate change**.
 
• Desertification leads to the loss of productive land, which has severe implications for the livelihood of the local population and the environment.
 
• Efforts to combat desertification include sustainable land management practices, reforestation, and policies aimed at reducing the impact of climate change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)** is an international agreement aimed at addressing desertification and mitigating the effects of drought.
 
• The Sahel region spans across several countries in Africa, including **Senegal, Mauritania, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Nigeria, Chad, Sudan, and Eritrea**.
 
• Desertification in the Sahel has been exacerbated by factors such as overgrazing, deforestation for fuelwood, and unsustainable farming practices.
 
• Climate change has contributed to more frequent and severe droughts in the Sahel, further accelerating the desertification process.
 
• Community-based initiatives and international cooperation are essential in addressing the challenges posed by desertification in the Sahel.

questions.question: If an atom has atomic number = 6 and number of neutrons = 10, then what is the atomic mass of the atom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atomic mass** is calculated as the sum of the number of protons and neutrons in an atom.
 
• For an atom with an **atomic number of 6**, it has 6 protons.
 
• Given that the number of neutrons is **10**, the atomic mass is the sum of protons and neutrons.
 
• Therefore, the atomic mass = 6 (protons) + 10 (neutrons) = **16**.
 
• The correct answer is **option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **atomic number** of an element is defined as the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The **number of neutrons** can vary in different isotopes of the same element, but the atomic number remains the same.
 
• The **atomic mass** is approximately equal to the mass number, which is the total number of protons and neutrons.
 
• In this example, the element with atomic number 6 is **Carbon**, and the isotope with 10 neutrons is known as Carbon-16.

questions.question: If the meat is cooked above 140°C, which of the following reactions occurs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maillard reaction**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Maillard reaction** is a chemical reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars that gives browned foods their distinctive flavor.
 
• This reaction typically occurs at temperatures above **140ºC** (284ºF).
 
• It is named after French chemist **Louis-Camille Maillard**, who first described it in the early 20th century.
 
• The Maillard reaction is crucial in the preparation of many foods, including meats, bread, and coffee, contributing to the development of complex flavors and aromas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Caramelisation** is another browning process that occurs when sugars are heated to high temperatures, but it does not involve amino acids like the Maillard reaction does.
 
• **Emulsification** is the process of mixing two immiscible liquids, such as oil and water, to form a stable mixture.
 
• **Oxidation reaction** involves the transfer of electrons between substances, often leading to changes in color and flavor, but it is not specific to the temperature mentioned.
 
• The Maillard reaction is responsible for the **distinctive taste and color** of browned foods and is a key factor in culinary practices.

questions.question:
Which of the following are the functions of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?

1) Providing Constitutional protection to Scheduled Castes

2) Investigating any case that violates the interests of Scheduled Castes

3) Submitting a report to the Prime Minister related to the protection of Scheduled Castes

4) Presenting to the President, annually and at such other times as the Commission may deem fit, reports upon the working of those safeguards
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1, 2 and 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) is an important body in India dedicated to the protection and welfare of Scheduled Castes (SCs). Let's analyze each function listed in the question to determine which are the correct responsibilities of the NCSC.
 
• **Providing Constitutional protection to Scheduled Castes** - This statement is correct. The NCSC is tasked with monitoring and investigating how the constitutional safeguards for SCs are implemented and adhered to. However, it does not directly provide these protections itself; its role is more supervisory and advisory.
 
• **Investigating any case that violates the interests of Scheduled Castes** - This is a correct function of the NCSC. According to Article 338 of the Indian Constitution, the commission has the power to investigate and monitor matters relating to the safeguards provided for SCs and to inquire into specific complaints regarding the deprivation of rights and safeguards of these communities.
 
• **Submitting a report to the Prime Minister related to the protection of Scheduled Castes** - This statement is incorrect. The NCSC submits its report to the President, not the Prime Minister. The commission presents reports on how the safeguards for SCs are being carried out, among other details.
 
• **Presenting to the President, annually and at such other times as the Commission may deem fit, reports upon the working of those safeguards** - This statement is correct. The NCSC is authorized to present annual reports to the President on the implementation of constitutional and other legal safeguards for SCs. The President then places these reports before each House of Parliament along with a memorandum explaining the action taken on the recommendations of the Commission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The NCSC was established under **Article 338** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Commission consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson, and three other Members appointed by the President of India.
 
• The NCSC is tasked with investigating and monitoring all matters relating to the constitutional and legal safeguards provided for the Scheduled Castes and evaluating the working of such safeguards.
 
• The Commission also participates and advises on the planning process of socio-economic development of the Scheduled Castes and evaluates the progress of their development under the Union and any State.
 
• It has the authority to inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Castes.

questions.question: The world's largest population of which endangered species resides in Assam's Kaziranga National Park?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-horned rhinoceros**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kaziranga National Park** in Assam is renowned for housing the world's largest population of the endangered **One-horned rhinoceros**.
 
• The park provides a crucial habitat for this species, playing a vital role in their conservation.
 
• As per the latest census, Kaziranga hosts more than 2,400 One-horned rhinoceroses, which is about two-thirds of their global population.
 
• The One-horned rhinoceros is also known as the Indian rhinoceros and is listed as vulnerable by the IUCN Red List.
 
• The park's efforts in anti-poaching and habitat management have significantly contributed to the increase in the rhino population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kaziranga National Park** is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its unique natural environment.
 
• Besides the One-horned rhinoceros, the park is also home to other wildlife such as tigers, elephants, and various species of birds.
 
• The park spans an area of approximately 430 square kilometers and is characterized by its tall elephant grass, marshland, and dense tropical moist broadleaf forests.
 
• Conservation efforts in Kaziranga are supported by various national and international organizations, ensuring the protection of its diverse ecosystem.
 
• The park attracts thousands of tourists annually, contributing to the local economy and raising awareness about wildlife conservation.

questions.question: What is the name of project undertaken by the Indian Government to conserve tigers when their population dwindled to very low numbers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Project Tiger**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Project Tiger** is a wildlife conservation project initiated by the Indian Government in 1973.
 
• The project aims to protect Bengal tigers from extinction by ensuring a viable population of tigers in their natural habitats.
 
• It focuses on maintaining a balance between tiger conservation and human development.
 
• The project has led to the establishment of numerous tiger reserves across India.
 
• It has been successful in increasing the tiger population in India over the years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Project Tiger** was launched on April 1, 1973, and is administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).
 
• The project is funded by the central government and aims to reduce factors that lead to the depletion of tiger habitats and to mitigate human-tiger conflicts.
 
• India is home to about 70% of the world's tiger population.
 
• The success of Project Tiger has inspired other countries to adopt similar conservation projects for their endangered species.

questions.question: What is a small, shallow freshwater body with calm water called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pond**__

__
 
• A small, shallow freshwater body with calm water is called a **pond**.
 
• Ponds are generally smaller than lakes and are often formed naturally or artificially.
 
• They provide habitats for various aquatic plants and animals.
 
• Ponds are typically found in landscapes such as gardens, parks, and agricultural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lakes** are larger and deeper bodies of freshwater compared to ponds.
 
• **Lagoons** are shallow bodies of saltwater separated from the sea by a barrier such as a sandbank or coral reef.
 
• **Rivers** are flowing bodies of water that usually originate from mountains or hills and flow towards a sea, ocean, or another river.

questions.question: What is the process by which one organism captures and consumes another organism called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Predation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Predation** is the process by which one organism, the predator, captures and consumes another organism, the prey.
 
• Predation is a biological interaction where a predator feeds on its prey, resulting in the death of the prey.
 
• This interaction plays a critical role in the ecosystem by regulating population sizes and maintaining ecological balance.
 
• Examples of predation include a lion hunting a zebra, a spider capturing an insect, and a hawk catching a mouse.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mutualism** refers to a relationship where both organisms benefit from the interaction.
 
• **Competition** occurs when two or more organisms vie for the same resource, such as food or territory.
 
• **Parasitism** involves one organism, the parasite, living on or in another organism, the host, causing it harm.
 
• Unlike predation, parasitism does not usually result in the immediate death of the host.

questions.question: The enzyme that is essential for fat digestion is:

• **Invertase** is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of sucrose into glucose and fructose.

questions.question: Which of the following features was borrowed by the Constitution of India from Ireland?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy** were borrowed by the Constitution of India from the Constitution of Ireland.
 
• These principles are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. They are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Directive Principles are mentioned in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• Though they are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by any court, they are fundamental in the governance and aim to establish a welfare state.
 
• The inspiration for these principles was drawn from the Irish Constitution, which was influenced by the Spanish Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.

• The revolt inspired subsequent agrarian movements in India and highlighted the need for agrarian reforms.

questions.question: Which system of India is based on the Westminster model?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Parliamentary system**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Parliamentary system** is based on the Westminster model.
 
• The Westminster model is a democratic parliamentary system of government modeled after the politics of the United Kingdom.
 
• It features a head of state, who is different from the head of government, and a parliament with two houses.
 
• In India, the President is the head of state, while the Prime Minister is the head of government.
 
• The Indian Parliament consists of two houses: the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• This system emphasizes the role of the Prime Minister and the Cabinet, who are accountable to the Lok Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Westminster model** originated in the United Kingdom and has been adopted by various countries, including India, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.
 
• The Indian Constitution was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, which was heavily influenced by the British system of governance.
 
• The Indian Parliamentary system ensures a separation of powers among the executive, legislative, and judicial branches of government.
 
• The system also incorporates a series of checks and balances to prevent any one branch from becoming too powerful.
 
• The Prime Minister and the Cabinet are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, which reflects the principle of collective responsibility.

questions.question: How many items did the Swaran Singh Committee recommend to be incorporated in the Constitution of India as duties of the Indian citizen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee recommended the incorporation of **8 duties** for Indian citizens in the Constitution of India.
 
• These recommendations led to the addition of Part IVA to the Constitution, which enumerates the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they should also be conscious of their duties towards the nation.
 
• The duties include respecting the Constitution, the national flag, and the national anthem, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, and upholding the sovereignty and integrity of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties is inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile Soviet Union.
 
• Initially, ten Fundamental Duties were listed, but the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added an eleventh duty, making it obligatory for parents to provide education to their children aged between 6 and 14 years.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties aims to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**The Swaran Singh Committee suggested eight items to be incorporated in the constitution as duties of the citizen. These are mentioned below:

 
• To respect and abide by the constitution and the laws.
 
• To uphold the sovereignty of the nation and to function in such a way as to sustain and strengthen its unity and integrity.
 
• To respect the democratic institutions enshrined in the constitution, and not to do anything which may impair their dignity or authority.
 
• To defend the country and to render national service including military service when called upon to do so.
 
• To abjure communalism in any form.
 
• To render assistance and cooperation to the State in the implementation of Directive Principles of State Policy, and to promote the common good of the people so as to sub serve the interests of social and economic justice.
 
• To abjure violence; to protect and safeguard public property and not to do anything which may cause damage or destruction to such property.
 
• To pay taxes according to the law.

However, then Congress government led by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi did not accept all suggestions or recommendations made by the Swaran Singh Committee.

questions.question: Boron is the only metalloid of which group of the periodic table?

• **Boron** is the only metalloid in **Group 13** of the periodic table.
 
• Group 13 elements are also known as the **boron group**, which includes boron (B), aluminum (Al), gallium (Ga), indium (In), and thallium (Tl).
 
• Among these elements, **boron** exhibits properties of both metals and non-metals, classifying it as a metalloid.
 
• Metalloids have intermediate properties and are often semiconductors, which boron also exhibits.
 
• Boron is essential for plant growth and has various industrial applications, including in borosilicate glass and detergents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Group 13** elements typically have three electrons in their outermost shell, leading to a +3 oxidation state in compounds.
 
• Boron compounds, such as borates, are used in glassmaking, ceramics, and as a mild antiseptic.
 
• Boron is also a component of boron nitride, a material with properties similar to carbon-based materials like graphite and diamond.
 
• In the periodic table, boron is located in period 2, making it the lightest element in Group 13.
 
• The unique properties of boron, such as its high melting point and hardness, make it useful in various high-temperature and abrasive environments.

questions.question: Which of the following fundamental rights has been amended as a constitutional right in the form of Article 300A in the new Chapter IV Part XII of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Property**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to Property** was originally a fundamental right under Article 31 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• However, the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of fundamental rights.
 
• It was then made a constitutional right under Article 300A in the new Chapter IV of Part XII of the Constitution.
 
• Article 300A states that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.
 
• This change was made to reduce the burden on the judiciary and to facilitate the process of land acquisition for public purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 31** was part of the original Constitution adopted on 26th November 1949.
 
• The **44th Amendment Act** was enacted during the Janata Party government led by Morarji Desai.
 
• The amendment aimed to balance the state's power to acquire property with the individual's right to hold property, without the stringent protections associated with fundamental rights.
 
• This amendment reflects the evolving nature of the Indian Constitution to address contemporary socio-economic needs.
 
• Other fundamental rights continue to be protected under Part III of the Constitution, ensuring justice, equality, and liberty for all citizens.

questions.question: In the context of internet access, Wi-Fi stands for ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wireless Fidelity**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wi-Fi** stands for **Wireless Fidelity**.
 
• Wi-Fi is a technology for wireless local area networking with devices based on the IEEE 802.11 standards.
 
• Wi-Fi is widely used in home and business networks, allowing electronic devices to connect to the internet or communicate wirelessly within a particular area.
 
• Wi-Fi networks use radio waves to transmit data and are typically secured with encryption protocols to protect data privacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wi-Fi Alliance** is a non-profit organization that promotes Wi-Fi technology and certifies Wi-Fi products for conformity to certain standards of interoperability.
 
• The term "Wi-Fi" was coined as a play on the term "Hi-Fi" (high fidelity), and it was meant to be an easier-to-remember brand name for the technology.
 
• Wi-Fi networks have become ubiquitous, providing internet access in various public and private spaces such as homes, offices, airports, and coffee shops.
 
• Wi-Fi technology continues to evolve, with newer standards offering faster speeds and more reliable connections.

questions.question: Which disease is characterised by the body's inability to regulate blood sugar levels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diabetes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diabetes** is a chronic disease that occurs either when the pancreas does not produce enough insulin or when the body cannot effectively use the insulin it produces.
 
• Insulin is a hormone that regulates blood sugar.
 
• There are three main types of diabetes: Type 1, Type 2, and gestational diabetes.
 
• Type 1 diabetes is characterized by insufficient insulin production and requires daily administration of insulin.
 
• Type 2 diabetes results from the body's ineffective use of insulin and is largely the result of excess body weight and physical inactivity.
 
• Gestational diabetes is hyperglycemia that is first recognized during pregnancy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The global prevalence of diabetes among adults over 18 years of age has risen from 4.7% in 1980 to 8.5% in 2014.
 
• In 2019, diabetes was the direct cause of 1.5 million deaths.
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends a healthy diet, regular physical activity, maintaining a normal body weight, and avoiding tobacco use to prevent or delay the onset of type 2 diabetes.
 
• Early diagnosis can be accomplished through relatively inexpensive blood testing.
 
• Treatment of diabetes involves diet and physical activity along with lowering blood glucose and the levels of other known risk factors that damage blood vessels.

questions.question: Under the Regulating Act of 1773, the Supreme Court was established by British Emperor in which of the following cities in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court was established in **Calcutta** under the Regulating Act of 1773.
 
• This act was enacted by the British Parliament to address the deficiencies in the administration of the British East India Company.
 
• The Supreme Court in Calcutta was the highest judicial authority in British India at that time.
 
• It marked the beginning of a structured judicial system in India, providing a foundation for subsequent legal and judicial developments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Regulating Act of 1773 was a significant step towards the centralization of British administration in India.
 
• It also led to the appointment of the Governor-General of Bengal, who had supervisory authority over the other British presidencies in India.
 
• The Act was one of the earliest attempts by the British government to regulate the affairs of the East India Company and its territories in India.
 
• The establishment of the Supreme Court aimed at ensuring justice and addressing the grievances of the local population as well as the British subjects in India.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan of ‘Do or Die’ during the ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quit India Movement**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan of **'Do or Die'** during the **Quit India Movement**__.
 
• The Quit India Movement was launched on **8th August 1942**, during World War II, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• It was a mass protest demanding what Gandhi called "an orderly British withdrawal" from India.
 
• The movement saw widespread acts of defiance and protests, including strikes, demonstrations, and the refusal to pay taxes.
 
• Despite the arrest of major leaders, the movement continued with the active participation of the masses, showcasing the strong desire for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Quit India Movement is also known as the **August Kranti** or August Movement.
 
• The British government responded with mass detentions and suppression of the movement, but it marked a significant phase in the Indian independence struggle.
 
• Gandhi's call for "Do or Die" motivated millions of Indians to participate actively in the freedom struggle, leading to a significant impact on the British decision to eventually leave India.
 
• The movement demonstrated the unity and determination of the Indian people to achieve self-rule and independence.

questions.question:
Which of the following sentence/s is/are NOT correct?

i. The detailed estimates of revenue receipts are usually presented in the finance bill.

ii. Non-tax revenue of the central government mainly consists of taxes imposed on goods imported into and exported out of India.

iii. Revenue receipts are redeemable.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ii and iii**__

• The detailed estimates of revenue receipts are usually presented in the budget, not the finance bill, making statement i incorrect.
 
• Non-tax revenue of the central government mainly consists of income from sources other than taxes, such as profits from public sector enterprises and interest receipts, not taxes on goods imported into and exported out of India. Therefore, statement ii is incorrect.</
